==Biography==
In ''[[The Sims 4]]'', the Grim Reaper wears an opaque black, modern cloak with a light gray hood and covering around his waist. With [[The Sims 4/Patch 174|Patch 174]], the front of the Grim Reaper's cloak is redesigned to expose his ribcage, making him more closely resemble his design in ''[[The Sims: Livin' Large]]'' and ''[[The Sims 2]]''. He will give unique answers when asked about his [[career]] or marital status. His [[trait (The Sims 4)|traits]] are randomized.

The Grim Reaper is featured during the [[Reward events|Reaper's Rewards event]], asking for [[Sim]]s for help making [[Ambrosia]].

The Grim Reaper can be seen outside reaping souls in the world of [[Ravenwood]], specifically within the [[neighborhood]] of [[Mourningvale]]. He is the boss of the [[Reaper]] career, where Sims can work for him at the [[Netherworld Department]].

==Gameplay mechanics==
[[File:Lest ye be reaped.png|thumb|right|The message that appears if the player attempts to plead with the Grim Reaper in ''[[The Sims 4]]'' before the reaping process has begun]]
When a [[Sim]] [[death|dies]], the Grim Reaper will appear from a cloud of smoke. He will consult his tablet before reaping the soul and replacing the body with an [[gravestone|urn]] or [[gravestone]].

Any living Sims on the lot can attempt to plead with the Grim Reaper, in which there is a 33% chance of the Grim Reaper bringing the Sim back to life or outright rejecting the plea.
*Sims who are [[fine]] or [[happy]] can normally plead for the Sim's life when the Grim Reaper appears. If successful, this plea will give the pleading Sim the "Saved Sim from Death" happy [[moodlet]], which lasts for 6 hours.
*Sims who are [[confident]] can demand the Grim Reaper to spare the Sim's life, with a 40% success chance. This increases to 50% if the pleading Sim is very confident. If successful, the pleading Sim will receive the "Commanded Death" confident moodlet, which lasts for 6 hours.
*Sims who are [[Flirty (emotion)|flirty]] can seduce the Grim Reaper to spare the Sim's life, with a 10% success chance (Increases to 20% success chance if the pleading Sim is very flirty). If successful, the pleading Sim will gain the "Seduced Death" confident moodlet, which lasts for 6 hours.
*Sims who are [[angry]] can yell at death, which will always be rejected.
*Sims who are [[sad]] can wail about the dying Sim's demise. There is a 30% chance this plea will work, which increases to 33% if the Sim has the [[gloomy]] [[trait (The Sims 4)|traits]], and 36% if the Sim has the gloomy trait and is very sad. The success chance for this plea increases to 40% if the Sim is very sad without the gloomy trait. If successful, the pleading Sim will gain the same moodlet they would using the normal plea.<ref>Pleading success chances and [[moodlet]]s are taken from ''[[The Sims 4]]'' source files.</ref>
*[[Child]] Sims have a better success rate at pleading than any other age.
*Sims with level 5 or more in [[mischief]] [[skill]] can "Toy with Death" using a [[voodoo doll]]. The Grim Reaper will lose the ability to reap Sim's life. The success chance will depend on how many times the Sim toys with Death before the Grim Reaper decides to reap the dying Sim.<ref>Details: In ''The Sims 4'', each time the [[Sim]] toys with Death, the Grim Reaper gains a little bit of "clemency" (This is tracked internally by the game). Once the Grim Reaper gains enough clemency, there will be a chance that the Reaper will spare the Sim. The more clemency the Reaper has, the greater the chance he will revive the [[death|dying]] Sim. Source: Taken from game data files.</ref>
*Sims can give the Grim Reaper a [[death flower]]. This is the only way to guarantee saving a dying Sim's life, and the only method, other than the voodoo doll, that does not grant Sims a moodlet if successful.
*If a Sim fails after drinking a Potion of Prompt Resurrection{{Vgversion|TS4:ROM}} and then the Sim dies, the Grim Reaper will always reject any plea, including giving him a death flower.
*If a Sim drinks the Reaper's Friend serum and dies within the next 24 hours, the Sim will be resurrected and instantly become good friends with the Grim Reaper.
*If a ghost uses the wishing well to wish for life and gets an overwhelmingly positive outcome resulting in being revived, that Sim will be resurrected should they die via any cause except [[death by old age|old age]] for the next 24 hours.
*If a Sim dies while having their familiar active, the Grim Reaper will resurrect them with a cool-down period.
*If a Sim dies within 24 hours after successfully drinking a [[potion]] of Prompt Resurrection, they will be revived before the Grim Reaper even comes.
*An evil chicken will [[fight (social type)|fight]] the Grim Reaper should its owner die.
*With ''[[The Sims 4: Life & Death|Life & Death]]'', Sims can try for a [[baby]] with the Grim Reaper, and their children will inherit the Grimborn trait. Subsequent [[family relationships|family]] members down the line also inherit a Descendant of Grim trait.

After the Grim Reaper is finished, there is a chance he may stick around on the [[lot]], on which other Sims can perform [[social interaction]]s on him. However, [[romantic (social type)|romantic]] [[interaction]]s generally will not go very far.

==Hints and tips==
===Move in===
The Grim Reaper can be moved into a [[household]] via [[testing cheats|testingcheatsenabled]]. Simply enable the [[cheats|cheat]], shift+click on the Grim Reaper before he leaves, and click "Add to Family"; this will allow the player to control him. When controllable, players are able to build up his romance bar, as he will be treated as a regular [[Sim]]. It is not possible to try for a [[baby]] with him. The Grim Reaper can't do some basic actions like sleeping, and instead of walking, he will "hover" towards his destination. None of his [[motive|needs]] except [[social]] and [[fun]] decay, so he does not need to sleep, wash, eat, or use the [[toilet]]. He also cannot feel [[sad]], and any [[moodlet]]s causing sadness will automatically be removed. If cheats are used to adjust his stats, the changes will stick and will not be reverted.

Playable Grim Reapers cannot be selected as a part of the group during meetings, if a Grim Reaper from a household is currently on another [[lot]], it cannot be ordered to come to current lot unless [[teleportation|teleported]] with modifications or selected on its current lot and ordered to travel, however, Grim Reapers can be invited by non-household Sims through a [[telephone|phone]], and Grim Reaper himself can invite other Sims on a meeting through a phone.

If a Sim [[death|dies]] after the Grim Reaper is added to a household using testingcheatsenabled, an additional Grim Reaper will be spawned to reap their soul. The new Grim Reaper can also be added to the household, and this process can be repeated to create a household with up to 8 Grim Reapers. Each Grim Reaper will have at least one [[trait (The Sims 4)|trait]] and a random [[aspiration (The Sims 4)|aspiration]].

Adding the Grim Reaper to a household will not cause any issues with the game.

==Biography==
The Grim Reaper's entire appearance is changed to fit the "Medieval" theme, such as changing his outfit from the color black to red, giving him small wings and purple hands with long nails instead of the bony ones and redoing his scythe. When the Grim Reaper appears, he will make the [[death|dead]] [[Sim]]'s spirit fly into the air. Then, he will disappear by going under the earth, taking the corpse Sim with him. In this game, he cannot be pleaded with for a Sim's life.

==Gameplay mechanics==
[[File:Grim Reaper tsm Pit.jpg|thumb|The Grim Reaper in ''[[The Sims Medieval]]'']]
The Grim Reaper has a totally different appearance in this stand-alone game. The Grim Reaper, like in every game, comes to collect the souls of the [[death|deceased]] [[Sim]]s. However, he doesn't stay around, like he usually does in ''[[The Sims 3]]'', and can't be made playable without the use of [[cheats]]. His appearance also appears to be very medieval, sporting bright colors along with the robes, a golden belt, and bright red caps.

A promotional picture seen to the right depicts a new Grim Reaper with a red robe, long white hair, black wings, a different scythe, and a belt with a skull and an hourglass on it. It is possible that it is the same Grim Reaper just dressing to fit the medieval theme of that era, or that he is the ancestor of all of the other Grim Reapers in the [[The Sims (series)|series]].

==Hints and tips==
===Move in===
The Grim Reaper can be moved into a [[household]] to get permanent control of him by enabling [[testing cheats|testingcheatsenabled]], shift-clicking on him, and then making him a spouse of the currently selected [[Sim]]. His [[hunger]] and [[energy]] [[motive]]s will not deplete, and he will be treated as a villager who does not [[fight (social type)|fight]]. He will usually possess the [[Evil (The Sims Medieval)|evil]] or [[morose]] [[trait (The Sims Medieval)|traits]]; his second trait will usually be randomized.
{{Warning-header|Making the Grim Reaper selectable in this manner has been known to cause problems with the game.}}

==Biography==
The Grim Reaper of ''[[The Sims 3]]'' has little backstory and only appears during [[death]] sequences, after moving in before the patch, through [[cheats]], or if the player owns The Door Of Life And Death ([[TheSims3.com#The Sims 3 Store|The Sims 3 Store]]). There is a [[statue]] of him in [[Pleasant Rest Graveyard]] in [[Sunset Valley]]. He wears a black hooded robe, and only his skeletal hands are visible underneath it. He has a very deep [[voice]] (provided by voice actor Will Blagrove at the lowest pitch), but if moved in, he will have voice 1 (provided by William Salyers) at an average pitch. In this game, a Sim can no longer plead for a deceased Sim's life, but after a certain patch, they can play [[chess table|chess]] with him and win. Forcing him to change his [[clothes]] will reveal that his [[skin#The Sims 3|skin]] tone is entirely black.

This Grim Reaper is depicted as being more cruel than his more neutral or sometimes his kindly portrayal in ''[[The Sims 2]]''. He acts coldly towards Sims who have recently died and those who plead with him. And while he may resurrect Sims with an [[unlucky]] [[trait (The Sims 3)|trait]], his reasoning behind it isn't altruistic - he finds their suffering to be too amusing to simply lay them to rest (he'll only do so if a Sim [[death by old age|dies of old age]]). His one exception is his treatment of [[animal]]s, as he'll show kindness towards recently departed [[pet]]s. In order to bring animals through a portal, presumably leading to the [[Netherworld]], he will throw toys and sticks for [[cat]]s and [[dog]]s to follow, and even ride [[horse]]s to lead them there.

==Gameplay mechanics==
[[File:Grimmy Pool Side.jpg|thumb|The Grim Reaper relaxing in a [[chair]]]]
[[File:Sims 3 Grim Reaper coming for drowned Sim.jpg|thumb|Grim reaper with a trident instead of a scythe]]
The Grim Reaper appears when a [[Sim]] or [[pet]] [[death|dies]]. However, unlike the previous games, the Grim Reaper will literally "reap" the spirit of the Sim to turn it into a [[ghost]], while the remaining Sims around the [[household]] or [[lot]] will mourn for him/her. The appearance of this ghost is determined by the cause of the death. When a Sim dies (not when the Grim Reaper is summoned by [[cheats]]), a special Grim Reaper Music will play.

[[File:Ressurect 2.png|thumb|The Grim Reaper forced to resurrect a [[Sim]] by a [[cat]]]]
With ''[[The Sims 3: Pets]]'', [[pet]]s can harass the Grim Reaper and save their master. The pet has to be at least best friends with the Sim to do this. There is a 35% chance pets will harass the Grim Reaper, and an additional +10% chance if they have [[aggressive]], [[loyal]], or [[Brave (pet)|brave]] [[trait (The Sims 3)|traits]]; or -10% if they have [[clueless]], [[Lazy (pet trait)|lazy]], [[nervous]], or [[skittish]] traits. A pet cannot save the same Sim from death more than once.

[[File:Grim reaper watching TV.png|thumb|right|The Grim Reaper watching [[television|TV]]]]
There is a 20% chance that he will stay for a short period of time after he's done with his job, and an additional +5% for each Sim that dies on the lot. The maximum chance is 75%. During this time, Sims may hang out and socialize with the Grim Reaper. The Grim Reaper will behave as if he were a guest, such as watching [[television|TV]] or using the [[toilet]]. He will not hang around if the Sim dies in a [[diving area]], however. If a Sim dies from a [[vending machine]],{{Vgversion|TS3:UL}} the Grim Reaper may attempt to buy a soda from the vending machine and drink from it. The soda will pass through his body and leave a [[puddle]] on the ground, which will remain after he leaves.

Some supernatural creatures, such as [[Vampire (The Sims 3)|vampires]], may be able to offer to turn the Grim Reaper. Even if this is accepted, it will not change the Grim Reaper in any way.

==Hints and tips==
===Move in===
It is possible to "Move In" the Grim Reaper into the active [[household]] without the use of any [[cheats]] or tools. What one needs is to build a [[relationship]] high enough with Grim Reaper when he lingers on the [[lot]] (this does not happen often) and ask him to move in. It's good to have the Legendary Host [[lifetime reward]]. He cannot be [[marriage|married]] and must be moved in. Having the [[charismatic]] [[Trait (The Sims 3)|trait]], maxed [[charisma]], charisma challenges completed, or the Never Dull lifetime reward can be very helpful here, as he disappears from the relationship panel when he leaves. Having the [[unlucky]] trait makes summoning him repeatedly much easier; otherwise, the player will only have one chance.

Another way to move in the Grim Reaper is to enable [[testing cheats|testingcheatsenabled]], shift-click on the [[mailbox]], make the selected [[Sim]] know everyone, and then invite the Grim Reaper over via the relationship panel. When he arrives, shift-click on him and add him to the current household. He will not be called the Grim Reaper and will simply become a regular Sim with black [[skin#The Sims 3|skin]] tone.

Take note that once he is moved in, he will disappear; this can be fixed by enabling testingcheatsenabled, shift-clicking anywhere in the world, and selecting "Teleport Here". He will have the first [[voice]] setting provided by William Salyers with an average pitch because he was generated like a new [[townie]]. Players can use cheats to change his voice back to the third voice setting provided by Will Blagrove with the lowest pitch by sending him back into [[Create a Sim]].

If ''[[The Sims 3: Late Night]]'' or later is installed, the Grim Reaper can no longer be moved in.

===Sim/Grim Reaper hybrids===
{{main|Hybrid#Reaper Spawn Glitch}}
It is possible in games patched below version 1.3 to try for a [[baby]] with the Grim Reaper without him being a [[family relationships|family]] member: after patch 1.3, the Grim Reaper must be a family member for such relations to be possible.

[[Hybrid]]s in ''[[The Sims 3]]'' can have totally black [[skin#The Sims 3|skin]] due to the Grim Reaper's unique [[genetics]]. The Grim Reaper can be added to the [[household]] by having a high [[relationship]] with him and asking him to move in. With [[testing cheats]], the player can drag the [[Sim]]'s relationship with the Grim Reaper to maximum instantly. After that, Sims can try to seduce the Grim Reaper until trying for baby [[interaction]] is available.

With the Door of Life and Death premium content from [[TheSims3.com#The Sims 3 Store|The Sims 3 Store]], it is possible to summon a Grim Reaper, build up a relationship with him, and then try for a baby with him. However, the Grim Reaper from the [[door]] is just a regular generated Sim, disguised as the Grim Reaper outfit. Trying for a baby with them does not make the Sim's offspring a Grim Reaper hybrid.

==Biography==
In the [[The Sims 2 (console)|console]] version of ''[[The Sims 2]]'', he has an identical appearance to the PC version, though he acts differently due to the different [[death]] mechanics in this version. [[Sim]]s are not made unplayable upon death, and end up as playable [[ghost]]s. The Grim Reaper will stay while a playable ghost is on the [[lot]].

Unlike most games, Sims cannot plead with him to save their loved ones. He can only be [[interaction|interacted]] with by ghost Sims. The Sim has an option to challenge him by playing the [[violin]] (if the Sim has high [[creativity (skill)|creativity]], [[charisma]], and [[logic]] [[skill]]s and has died in a Platinum mood, they have higher chances of winning) or pay him §100 to return to life. In either case, the Sim will be resurrected, and the Grim Reaper will burn and disappear.

==Gameplay mechanics==
All [[Sim]]s that [[death|die]] will be reborn as [[ghost]]s, where they can find the Grim Reaper standing at the front of the [[lot]]. They can then challenge him to a fiddle contest. Sims that have a higher [[creativity (skill)|creativity]] [[skill]] and have died when in Platinum mood have a higher chance of winning. If the Sim wins, then the Grim Reaper will disappear.

As a [[ghost]], the Sim is more likely to have the [[aspiration (The Sims 2)|aspiration]] goals of:
*Good: To return to life
*Bad: To fail the fiddle challenge (to lose against Death).
If the player wishes not to choose the fiddle challenge or simply gives up, they can pay a fee of §100 to return to life.

==Biography==
''[[The Sims Life Stories]]'' is the only game in ''[[The Sims Stories]]'' series where the Grim Reaper serves as an important character in [[Story mode (The Sims Stories)|Story Mode]]. In the final chapter of [[Vincent's story]], he comes to reap [[Naomi Hunt]]'s life after she is hit by a falling [[satellite]] until [[Vincent Moore]] begs him to save her. The Grim Reaper then offers Vincent a choice: he must forfeit [[List of Bitville lots#1 JCN Circle|his mansion]] and his wealth in exchange for Naomi's life, or let her [[death|die]] so he can keep his fortune. The Grim Reaper's only other appearance in Story Mode is in the [[Shipwrecked and Single]] story in ''[[The Sims Castaway Stories]]'', where [[Bart Pittman]] dies moments after meeting the player's [[Sim]]; the Grim Reaper plays a minor role in reaping Bart's life, the player's Sim, having no [[relationship]] with him, is unable to plead with the Grim Reaper for his life.

==Gameplay mechanics==
In ''[[The Sims Life Stories]]'', if a [[Sim]] successfully saves a Sim from the Grim Reaper, a message from the Grim Reaper will appear at the top right of the screen saying "You intrigue me, mortal, I am going to hang out here for a while to find out how you beat me." The Sim who defeated the Grim Reaper will then greet the Grim Reaper, and then the Grim Reaper will stay at the Sim's house for a while and play [[chess table|chess]].

==Biography==
In ''[[The Sims 2]]'', the Grim Reaper's appearance is different from that in other games: he is gray and wraithlike rather than skeletal and black. His voice is very deep and unique to him. [[Olive Specter]] has [[memories]] of [[WooHoo]] with him and giving [[pregnancy|birth]] to [[Nervous Subject]] shortly after, though this is impossible in normal gameplay. Through the use of [[cheats]], a [[biography]] of him can be seen, containing some tongue-in-cheek information. With the ''[[The Sims 2: University|University]]'' [[Content pack#Expansion pack|expansion pack]], he can be bribed to resurrect [[death|dead]] [[Sim]]s with the [[Resurrect-O-Nomitron]], which is the [[career rewards|career reward]] for the [[Paranormal#The Sims 2|Paranormal]] [[career]] track. If the last Sim on the lot dies, one of a variety of sardonic messages will appear. On occasion, he will [[interaction|interact]] with one of the items in the house before leaving. So far, he has only been known to get a blended drink from a minibar, watch [[television]], relax on a [[bed]], use the [[toilet]], and/or play on the [[computer]]. Despite other games depicting the Grim Reaper as masculine, but in ''The Sims 2'' the Grim Reaper is treated as feminine. This is why they use a feminine portrait pose; however, the game uses masculine pronouns to refer to him in the "Game Over" messages.

When a Sim dies prematurely, the Grim Reaper browses through a list to find the Sim's name on it and makes a [[telephone|phone]] call. A beam of light appears above the dead Sim and turns them into a [[gravestone|grave]].

When Sims [[death by old age|die of old age]], there are two life endings they can get, based on their [[aspiration (The Sims 2)|aspiration]]. If they have any [[aspiration bar|aspiration level]] from failure to green, the Grim Reaper will come with a black trail of smoke and hold up an empty hourglass, meaning that the Sim has no more time to live. The Sim will then try to grab the hourglass out of Death's hand and try to flip it back over. The Grim Reaper then snatches it back and angrily points in a direction. The Sim walks there, and an [[gravestone|urn]] or grave (plain gray) is created. If the dying Sim is in gold or platinum aspiration, Death will come wearing a pink Hawaiian lei and will have a white smoke trail. Two [[Hula Zombie]]s will appear, and relaxing Hawaiian music will play. Death will slowly point at the dying Sim in a non-angry way, and the Sim will back up and act shy. Death will then hold his arms out as if to hug the Sim, then will give them a tiki glass with a lemon on the side. Then Death will pack the Sim's bags, and the Sim, still being timid, will smile and slowly head off to the afterlife. If the Sim was in platinum aspiration, their urn or grave will be gold and white and will show the symbol for their aspiration.

In general, when two Sims in a [[household]] are scheduled to die on the same day, the Grim Reaper will first come for one and will come back later for the other. However, if both members of a [[marriage|married]] or joined couple are scheduled to die on the same day, he may take both at once.

The Grim Reaper will not come if a Sim is eaten by a [[Laganaphyllis simnovorii|cow plant]].{{Vgversion|TS2:U}}

==Gameplay mechanics==
[[File:Plead grim.jpg|thumb|The Plea in ''[[The Sims 2]]'']]
The Grim Reaper can be pleaded with as in ''[[The Sims: Livin' Large|Livin' Large]]''; however, the chance of success is directly linked to the [[relationship]] score of the pleader to the [[death|deceased]]: if the total of the daily and lifetime relationship is below 25, the plea is guaranteed to fail. If it is above that level, the percentage chance of the plea succeeding is equal to that same number, which is capped at 90. If the plea succeeds, the [[Sim]] is "Saved From Death", which is frequently a major [[Wants and Fears|want]] for [[Knowledge]] Sims. 

There are a few scenarios in which Sims cannot plead with the Grim Reaper. If the death is from [[Death by old age|old age]], the plea [[interaction]] will be unavailable. If a Sim is eaten by a [[Laganaphyllis simnovorii|Cowplant]], it will immediately spit out a [[gravestone]], and the Grim Reaper will not appear. Sims must be able to reach the Grim Reaper to plead with him; if a Sim [[Drowning|drowns]] too far from the edge of a [[swimming pool|pool]], this interaction will not be available.

In ''[[The Sims 2: University|University]]'', the [[Resurrect-O-Nomitron]] [[Career rewards#Paranormal|reward]] from the [[Paranormal]] [[career]] enables Sims to call the Grim Reaper and pay him to bring back Sims with whom they have a relationship. The precise results depend on the payment:

*A payment of §1 - §987 will cause the resurrection to fail and the [[simoleon|money]] to be lost to no effect.
*A payment of §988 - §4127 will cause the dead Sim to return as a [[zombie]], losing most of their [[skill]]s, with a set [[personality]] (outgoing 4, active 3, playful 1), and with a negative [[mood]] and loss of relationship towards their resurrector.
*A payment of §4128 - §8512 will cause the dead Sim to return exactly as they looked, but with their personality inverted, a different job or a demotion, and some points lost from each skill (the lower the bid, the worse the effect). They will have a modest relationship boost to their resurrector.
*A payment of §8513 - §10,000 will result in the deceased Sim returning in perfect condition, exactly as when they died (but reset to start of age range they were in) and in a good mood.
*If the dead Sim in question is a [[child]] (or a [[pet]]), the resurrection will always succeed perfectly regardless of payment, with the Grim Reaper stating that he loves kids. (Children cannot become zombies in ''[[The Sims 2]]''.)

In ''[[The Sims 2: FreeTime]]'', Sims may ask the [[genie]] to give them the power to cheat death. This enables them to plead for their own life with a 100% chance of success the first time, which decreases by 10% with each subsequent attempt. Sims who die of old age will only be given one day of life before dying of old age again. In ''[[The Sims 2: Apartment Life]]'', good [[witch]]es with level 9 magic skill and the correct ingredients can cast the Expello Mortis [[spells (The Sims 2: Apartment Life)|spell]] to banish the Grim Reaper, saving a dying Sim. Also, an evil witch with 9 magic skill points and correct ingredients can cast the Vivificus Zombiae spell at the tombstone or [[gravestone|urn]] of a Sim, and the Sim will return as a zombie.

==Biography==
In addition to his appearance when a [[Sim]] [[death|dies]], he will also appear and ring the doorbell if there are more than five Jack-O-Lanterns on the [[lot]], a reference to trick-or-treating. There is a suggested malevolence about him, as can be seen from the results when Sims plead with him. [[Bonehilda]] is a huge fan of the Grim Reaper and will try to get an autograph from him when he's present while she's out of her [[closet]]. When the Grim Reaper appears, he will move over to the dead Sim and wave his scythe, and any [[adult]] Sim can plead with the Grim Reaper and attempt to save the Sim's life. If the Grim Reaper is in a bad [[mood]], the Sim will die regardless. If the Grim Reaper is in a good mood, however, he will challenge the pleading Sim to a game of rock, paper, scissors — if the pleading Sim loses, the dead Sim will be resurrected as a [[zombie]]; if they win, however, the Sim will be fully resurrected.

==Gameplay mechanics==
[[File:Plea Sims 1.jpg|thumb|The Plea in ''[[The Sims]]'']]
The Grim Reaper will appear in a cloud of skulls next to the [[mailbox]], then walk over to the [[death|dying]] [[Sim]] and spend a short amount of time waving his scythe. If the path to the dying Sim is blocked, he will [[teleportation|teleport]] there instead.

During this time, another Sim may be directed to approach and plead with him. This option is not available for [[child]]ren. There is around a 50% chance of him accepting the plea, at which point he will play a game of rock-paper-scissors with the pleader. If the Sim loses, there is still a 50% chance of him bringing the deceased back to life as a [[zombie]], with their skin-colored green and their [[personality]] wiped. Usually, the Grim Reaper will be in a bad [[mood]] and turn down the plea, and the Sim will die, but they will come back as a [[ghost]], being see-through and greenish-blue and walk around "spooking" Sims and making windy ghost noises.

If ''[[The Sims: Livin' Large|Livin' Large]]'' is not installed, the Grim Reaper will not appear; instead, the dying Sim will spawn a [[gravestone]] automatically. Regardless of whether ''Livin' Large'' is installed or not, this will also always happen if the Sim dies in the [[Skydiving simulator|Skydiving Simulator]] in ''[[The Sims: Superstar|Superstar]]'', or if a Sim is turned into a [[toad]] and subsequently eaten by a [[dragon]] or [[cat]] in ''[[The Sims: Makin' Magic|Makin' Magic]]''.

The Grim Reaper also appears in {{WP|SimGolf}} as a downloadable golfer. Fittingly, most of his dialog is morbid and alludes to the [[death]] of himself or his golf partner, as well as his skeletal appearance.

On November 25, 2024, ''[[The Sims (series)|The Sims]]'' launched its collaboration with the animated video app [[Frever]]. The Grim Reaper is used in some of the promotional materials for the collaboration.<ref>https://www.instagram.com/reel/DCzYpcASmaU/</ref>

The Grim Reaper appears in the console versions of ''[[The Sims]]'' and ''[[The Sims: Bustin' Out]]''. He appears similarly to his appearance in ''[[The Sims: House Party]]'', though his icon in those games shows a white skull in a black cloak robe. He appears whenever a [[Sim]] dies due to a [[fire]] and comes to collect their spirit. As in the PC version, the Grim Reaper can be pleaded with by Sims to attempt to have a dead Sim get a second chance at life. In [[Game guide:Get a Life mode walkthrough|Get a Life]] mode, if he reaps the soul of a dead Sim, a [[game over]] will result, and the player will lose all progress and be forced to start over from the beginning or from the last save game.

The Grim Reaper was added to ''[[The Sims FreePlay]]'' in the "Life Dreams" update.

==Trivia==
*The Grim Reaper, along with [[Mortimer Goth]], [[Bella Goth]], [[Betty Newbie]], [[Bob Newbie]], [[Daniel Pleasant]], and [[Agnes Crumplebottom]] are the only pre-made characters to appear in all four of the main [[The Sims (series)|series]] games.    
**He is one of the only two pre-made characters who is an [[Non-playable character|NPC]] in all four games of the main series, along with Agnes Crumplebottom. Alongside that, The Grim Reaper, Agnes Crumplebottom, [[Bonehilda]], and the [[Tragic Clown]] are the only NPCs from ''[[The Sims]]'' and its [[Content pack#Expansion pack|expansion packs]] to make an appearance in any of the sequels.
*Although appearing in almost all games, he was replaced by different characters in several games. In ''[[The Urbz: Sims in the City]]'' for [[The Urbz: Sims in the City (console)|console]], he was replaced with [[Captain Catastrophe]], who will, rather than take the life, save the [[Sim]] with shock pads. In ''[[The Sims Bustin' Out (handheld)|The Sims Bustin' Out (Handheld)]]'', ''[[The Urbz: Sims in the City (handheld)|The Urbz (Handheld)]]'', ''[[The Sims 2]]'', and ''[[The Sims 2: Pets|The Sims 2 Pets]]'' for the portable consoles, he is replaced with a [[genie]], who will save the Sim, although he laughs at their misery first. In ''The Sims 2 Pets'' for non-portable consoles, he is replaced by the [[Paramedic]], who will revive any unconscious Sims after a certain amount of time.
*In ''[[The Sims Bustin' Out]]'' for [[The Sims Bustin' Out (console)|console]]'', the Grim Reaper can be eaten by the [[Mutant plant]] but it won't kill them. Also, male [[voice]] clips are used if such an event happens.
*In ''The Sims 2'', there is only one Grim Reaper, and the game will not regenerate him if he is moved into or [[marriage|married]] into a [[household]]. This will also cause [[Game guide:Avoiding corruption|game corruption]] in ''The Sims 2''.
*In all ''Sims'' games except for ''[[The Sims 4]]'', the Grim Reaper will not react to a [[fire]]. However, in some rare cases in ''[[The Sims 3]]'', he will stay and put out the fire.

===The Sims===  
*In ''[[The Sims]]'', if the Grim Reaper comes during a [[fire]], it is possible for him to catch on fire, wherein the game will temporarily treat him as a normal [[Sim]], and he may perform the panic animation, and even [[death|die]]. If he does, the player can briefly see him in a dark, naked human [[skin#The Sims|skin]], still wearing his hood. He will immediately respawn a few tiles away and return to reaping Sims.
*In ''The Sims'' for [[The Sims (console)|consoles]], if you evict the [[family relationships|family]] of a Sim who's dying and then move them back, an eerie sound will be playing.

===The Sims 2 === 
*In ''[[The Sims 2]]'', his favorite band, Styx, is a real-life progressive rock band, whose name is a reference to the river in the underworld of Greek mythology.
*On one of the Grim Reaper dialogs, it states the Grim Reaper's [[zodiac sign]] is a Taurus; however, his sign is actually Cancer.
*In ''The Sims 2'' for [[The Sims 2 (console)|consoles]], a Sim can play the [[violin]] against the Grim Reaper. This is a reference to the song ''Devil Went Down to Georgia''.
*The Grim Reaper appears to be disappointed or annoyed when a Sim [[death|dies]] prematurely, as he shakes his head, mumbles something, and sighs while looking at the dead Sim.
*The Grim Reaper's mobile [[telephone|phone]] displays a skull.
*While the Grim Reaper's zodiac sign is Cancer when added to the family, one [[game over]] screen states he is a Taurus.
*When all Sims in the family die, a message called "The Finale" will appear, seemingly addressed to the player from Grim himself.
**He may simply state all members of the family have died, and encourage the player to move in a new family.
**After questioning what can be said about Death, he'll say he is a Taurus, enjoys taking long walks across the beach, loves [[horse]]s and prefers a woman with a horse over one with a SUV while also noting anyone interesting should be "gravely serious" about a [[relationship]].
**If too many Sims die in a very short time, the Grim Reaper will get angry, stating that this game is a life simulator. He will then humorously state the player can either exit without saving or move in another family, suggesting the player was deliberately trying to kill the sims. 
*Similarly, if all Sims aged [[teen]] and above die, and there are still [[child]]ren or younger on the lot, a message from Grim called "The Orphanage Awaits" appears. 
**In one, he'll reference Charles Dickens' novels and the song "It's a Hard Knock Life" from the musical ''Annie'', before saying they'll eventually hopefully be [[adoption|adopted]] by some wealthy benefactor.
**He'll explain that the children's house was put up for sale by the SimCity Orphan Tax Collection Agency to cover the care of the orphaned children, before expressing sadness at the fact the child will not find a huge, unknown [[inheritance]]. 
**The Grim Reaper will say conditions in the orphanage have improved, saying 10 years ago they were "serving reconstituted gruel cooked over tire [[fire]]s" before humorously saying the smell of such [[cooking]] still remains but managerial raises have risen.

===The Sims 3=== 
*In ''[[The Sims 3]]'', a [[Sim]] can play [[chess table|chess]] with the Grim Reaper to resurrect the [[death|dying]] Sim. This is a reference to the movie ''The Seventh Seal'' or making a deal with Lord Loss from Darren Shan's Demonata.
*A new Grim Reaper is generated at the start of each save file, resulting in each Grim Reaper having slightly different [[trait (The Sims 3)|traits]] and [[favorite]]s. He will always have at least one trait encouraging mean behavior, such as [[Evil (The Sims 3)|evil]], [[mean spirited]], or [[inappropriate]].
*When using the Door of Life And Death from [[TheSims3.com#The Sims 3 Store|The Sims 3 Store]], challenging the Grim Reaper to a [[guitar]] duel may be a reference to the guitar duel scene in Tenacious D's Pick of Destiny.
*In ''The Sims 3'', the music that plays when the Grim Reaper comes is similar to the {{WP|Imperial March}} from {{WP|The Empire Strikes Back|Star Wars: The Empire Strikes Back}}.
*If a Sim gets killed by a [[vending machine]], the Grim Reaper will briefly show up just as the machine flattens them. After reaping their soul, he will grab a drink from that vending machine and pour it at the site of a Sim's death to pay his respects.

===The Sims 4===
*The Grim Reaper has a book chained onto his waist, as well as a skeleton-themed [[Freezer Bunny]].
*The Grim Reaper may pet or play with a [[laganaphyllis simnovorii|cowplant]] on the [[lot]] after a [[Sim]] has [[death|died]], or use a [[Karaoke machine]].
*If the player pauses the game while the camera is locked on the Grim Reaper, there is a chance eerie music will play even though the game is paused.
*When coming to reap a Sim's soul, the Grim Reaper has a tablet. This could be a reference to the depiction of the god of death Thanatos in ''The Son of Neptune'', the second novel in the ''Heroes of Olympus'' series by Rick Riordan.
*If one takes a close look at the tablet he's holding, one can see the large [[gravestone]] from ''[[The Sims 3]]''. The gravestone's color implies that it is a [[fire]] gravestone.
*The Grim Reaper has an exclusive [[Secrets (The Sims 4)|secret]] with ''[[The Sims 4: For Rent]]'' installed called "Being Grim".
*In the trailer for ''[[The Sims 4: Lovestruck]]'', the Grim Reaper enjoys a flirtatious exchange with [[Don Lothario]], suggesting that both Sims are [[attraction|attracted]] to men.
*The Grim Reaper has the most [[interaction]]s in [[The Sims (series)|''The Sims'' series]] in ''[[The Sims 4: Life & Death]]'', where he is the boss of the reaper [[career]]. It also includes the world of Ravenwood, in which Grim can be seen every now and then roaming within the [[neighborhood]] of [[Mourningvale]], which is one of the few times Grim can be found outside of a Sim's recent death or being summoned. Those who are in the reaper career can have the luxury of "seeing" Grim under his hood.
*With the Regal Treasures Digital Content [[Limited expansion items|early purchase incentive]] for ''[[The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy]]''; the Enemies to Lovers [[Training dummy#Enemies to Lovers Practice Dummy|Practice Dummy]]'s second swatch is the Grim Reaper.

[[File:The Sims House Party Logo.png|80px|left]]
'''''The Sims: House Party''''' is the second [[expansion pack]] released on March 28, 2001 for ''[[The Sims]]''.

{{clrl}}
__TOC__
==Features==
===New objects===
* [[Buffet table|Catering table]]
* [[Dance floor]]
* [[Drink fountain]]
* [[Bar (object)|Themed bars]], turntables and [[fireplace]]s
* [[Campfire]]
* [[DJ booth]]
* [[Bubble bar]]
* [[Porta-Parody Costume Trunk|Costume Trunk]]

===New NPCs===
* '''[[Entertainer]]s''': Buy a large cake, and hidden inside is a [[party dancer]], they are sexy, both male and female. But if a kid is at home, a gorilla will appear instead. They will [[flirt]] with your Sims, married or single!
* '''[[Drew Carey]]''': He will appear if you're throwing a great party. He will come to your home in a [[limousine]].
* '''[[Green Beard the Ghost]]''': Have a [[Creativity (skill)|creative]] Sim tell a good story around the campfire, and a ghost might appear!
* '''[[Mime]]''': Throwing a bad party? The mime is here to crash the party and try to make it better. Beware of his hands, though, as he will steal items from your home!
* '''[[Caterer]]''': Hire a caterer to keep the plates full at the debutante ball.
* '''Party crashers''': [[Pete Dropinsky|Pete]] or [[Paulette Dropinsky|Paulette]] might drop in when a party starts getting good.

===New building themes===
*Western country saloons
*Hawaiian Tiki
*The electronic rave.

===Other new features===
* '''[[party|House party]]''': [[Sim]]s can throw a party, and invite a large number of Sims to their house.
* '''New [[Soundtrack Music]]''': Rap, Techno, Country Dance, Beach, and Disco
* '''New [[clothes|costumes]]''': From togas to beachwear, all are available if your Sims wanted to throw a Greek party or beach party.
* Roasting marshmallows, sing, and tell ghost stories with a campfire.
*[[DJ booth]]s, dance floors, buffet table and many more new objects!

==Critical Reception==
''The Sims: House Party'' received an average reception from both critics and players. Critics praised the new party gameplay, mechanics and objects while criticizing the limited gameplay value and content additions compared to ''[[The Sims: Livin' Large]]'', with some questioning whether the pack justified a commercial release. Criticism was also noted stating that the expansion did not change the basic structure of the game or add any significant gameplay additions as well as the time and financial management making parties hard to manage. Positive reception was aimed at the NPCs, including the cake dancers and [[Drew Carey]], the latter frequently mentioned by players as one of the most memorable real world celebrities to have appeared in the franchise. Many players have considered ''The Sims: House Party'' to be the least feature filled expansion pack for ''The Sims'' as well as one of the least feature filled expansion packs in the franchise, with some stating that the pack is not an essential purchase for gameplay value. 

==Trivia==
* ''The Sims: House Party'' is the first expansion pack to introduce townies.
* ''The Sims: House Party'' is the only expansion pack for ''[[The Sims]]'' to change its cover during its manufacturing period as well as one of two expansion packs from the first three games to change its cover during its manufacturing period, the second one being ''[[The Sims 2: University]]''.
* Starting from this expansion pack, a video for both the [[Electronic Arts|EA Games]] logo and the [[Maxis]] logo precedes the intro video and splash screen for the game instead of a static graphic for the 1992 Maxis logo as in the original base game. In this variant, the 2000 EA Games logo animation fades out to black to fade into the Maxis logo, while soundbites of Sims cheering are played in the audio. This logo combo is retained in [[The Sims: Vacation|''The Sims: Vacation'']], [[Compilations of The Sims#The Sims: Deluxe Edition|''The Sims: Deluxe Edition'']], and [[The Sims: Unleashed|''The Sims: Unleashed'']].

[[File:TS4 Career Freelancer.png|45px]] The '''freelancer''' career was added to ''[[The Sims 4]]'' via [[The Sims 4/Patch 79|patch 79]]. Sims don't progress through career levels but instead select an agency that helps connect them to individual gigs.

The freelancer career functions similarly to [[skill career]]s in ''[[The Sims 3]]'' in that there is no workplace. Sims work on their own time from home, and level up after doing a certain number of gigs.

Good-natured gigs (such as creating art for a charity) will raise a Sim's [[reputation]]{{Vgversion|GF}}, whereas bad-natured gigs (such as forging art for a suspicious client) will lower their reputation.

'''Rory Oaklow''' is a pre-made [[werewolf]] [[townie]] residing in [[Moonwood Mill]], the [[world]] shipped with ''[[The Sims 4: Werewolves]]''. She does not live in a house, but can be found in [[Manage Worlds]]. She is the alpha [[werewolf]] of [[Werewolf pack#The Wildfangs|The Wildfangs]] [[Werewolf pack|wolf pack]].

Rory is a [[young adult]], 25 days away from becoming an [[adult]].

==Backstory==
Rory's biography states that she decided to form the pack herself following an ideological split from her adoptive father and former mentor, [[Kristopher Volkov]], but she still has a lot to learn. Unlike her relationship with her adoptive father, she still has a good relationship with her adoptive brother [[Jacob Volkov|Jacob]], whom she misses. She has also appeared in several promotional materials for ''Werewolves'', as well as the reveal trailer.

Rory was born a normal human Sim and raised in a normal human family; before arriving in Moonwood Mill, she had never met a [[Spellcaster]]. According to Kristopher, her childhood was not a happy one. She still has yet to meet the infamous [[vampire]] [[Vladislaus Straud]], but wishes to fight him when she does, to assert dominance. Her philosophy on Fury is that if it is an ocean, then the Moonwood Collective stays on dry land, [[Greg]] is drowning in it, and her Wildfangs are happy to swim in it when it suits them. Fittingly, if Rory were not a werewolf, she would want to be a [[mermaid]]. 

Physical [[Fitness (skill)|fitness]] is very important to Rory, and she and her fellow Wildfangs are responsible for converting a wing of the Moonwood Mill [[library]] to a makeshift [[gym]]. She endorses the importance of keeping fit to a woman named Maura in the description of the [[weight machine]] that was included with the pack, which she is implied to have built herself.

Despite her ideological differences with the Moonwood Collective, Rory does not inherently dislike their ideals. She believes they have helped her younger brother, but that they do not personally work for her.

==[[Ask About Moonwood Mill Replies|"Ask About Moonwood Mill" Replies]]==
===0–35 Relationship Points===
*If I wasn't a Werewolf, I think I'd want to be a Mermaid. Surprised? Eh, don't be. They also have a connection to the moon, you know? With the tides and all that. Did you know mermaids can stay out of the water longer during a Full Moon?
*The Moonwood Collective fears their own natural state. It's like they've built a fire that they only let smolder. Why not stoke that thing and have some fun? Just keep it contained to the fire pit, you know?
*What are the Wildfangs about? All right, think of fury like the ocean. The Moonwood Collective wants to avoid it. Greg is drowning in it. The Wildfangs want to go for a swim. Sure, it's not 100% safe, but can you imagine living your whole life by the water and never taking a dip?
*We may not be in the same pack anymore, but I love my little brother, Jacob. Always have, always will. And I think the Moonwood Collective suits him well. It just didn't work for me.
*Just because I'm all about embracing the inner beast doesn't mean I'm opposed to someone seeking a cure. Be true to you. That's what's important. Just don't try to make me take it!

===35–60 Relationship Points===
*I've never had a fated mate before. And even if fate decided to put me on the list, I don't really subscribe to that being the end-all-factor in who I end up with. I decide my fate.
*Even as a kid, I had a strong sense of individuality. Yeah, Kristopher is my dad, but I've always been Rory Oaklow, you know? I'm not going to change my name for some elder Werewolf. Jacob wanted to. That's his decision, and I support that.
*Other occults come here from time to time. Before coming here, I'd never met a Spellcaster! I was always around normie Sims, born and raised in a standard normie family. It's strange to think about now. I wouldn't want to go back to that.
*Sure, normies are great, but they're not my pack, and they can never be. That's fine. You're close with the people you connect with, you run with the ones you trust, you know?
*What would I do if I ever met Vlad Straud? I'd fight him, of course. He needs to know who the top dog around here is. And it's not going to be some ancient, evil Vampire.

===60–100 Relationship Points===
*I don't talk much about my past. I was bit by a dog that'd somehow contracted lycanthropy. It doesn't usually happen, so it must have been a freak accident. I was with my family at the vet in Brindleton Bay—that's where I grew up. The day after my first transformation, my parents kicked me out. They didn't know how to handle the new me. Kristopher took me in. We don't agree on a lot of things these days, but I'll always remember his kindness.
*When I became leader of a pack, I realized I was going to have to open myself to learning about what it means to be a leader each day. There's always a lot of pressure to care for the well-being of those who follow me, but I want to do right by the pack.
*I learned the secrets to immortality early. Most werewolves don't, but I was able to by truly embracing who I am inside. I don't hide, and because of that, I'm more in tune with my inner wolf.
*Kristopher thinks that if I keep heading down the path I'm on, I'll turn out like Greg. He can't be serious. I'm nothing like Greg. I'm in control. I just don't shy away from the fury inside me. I use it. Sure, it's a difficult balancing act, but I'm killing it.
*The original Werewolves didn't deny their inner beasts. They embraced the moon and its magic, and they used it for good, keeping the Vampires from taking over. I don't think the Moonwood Collective would even be strong enough today to take on the Vampires if they started another conflict. The Wildfangs would be.<ref>https://www.tumblr.com/adelarsims/790967322295828480/moonwood-mill-gossip</ref>

Olive Specter.title: Olive Specter
Olive Specter.text:
{{Era|TS2|TS3SE|TS3MH|TS4|TS4L&D|FA}}
{{DEFAULTSORT:Specter, Olive}}
'''Olive Specter''' {{Nee|Muenda}} (''previously'' '''Mortis''' ''and'' '''Thanasia''') is one of the pre-made playable [[Sim]]s featured in ''[[The Sims 2]]'' and ''[[The Sims 4: Life & Death]]''.

She and her orphaned [[teen]] niece, [[Ophelia Specter|Ophelia Nigmos]], reside in the [[Specter family|Specter]] household in the [[neighborhood]] of [[Strangetown]]. Olive is a many-time widow - her many husbands included [[Hugh Thanasia]], [[Rigger Mortis]], and [[Ichabod Specter]] (all are [[death|deceased]] before the game begins). She was also left at the altar by [[Earl E. DeMise]], who died soon after. The death of her many husbands has led some players to [[Olive Specter/theories|theorize]] that Olive is a murderer or was somehow responsible for their deaths; these theories remain unconfirmed.

She later appeared as a younger version of herself alongside her son [[Nervous Subject]] in the store world [[Midnight Hollow]].

==Biography==
In the [[Timeline of events in The Sims series#Alternate timeline|alternate timeline]] of ''[[The Sims 4]]'', Olive lives in [[Crow's Crossing]] with her new fiancé [[Layne Coffin]] and son [[Nervous Subject|Nyon Specter]], who was known as [[Nervous Subject]] in the original timeline and was taken away by the [[Social Worker]] before he was a [[child]]. This name change is explained by his not being experimented on by the [[Beaker family]] yet in the alternate timeline. The developers described him as "pre-Nervous," suggesting it takes place before he met the Beakers and became Nervous Subject.<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfV7shwdWus</ref> Olive is an [[adult]], 42 days away from becoming an [[elder]].

==Social==
===[[File:Ravenwood Rumors.png|30px|link=]] Ravenwood Rumors===
Olive, like other citizens of Ravenwood, has a special interaction called ''Ravenwood Rumors'' that reveals tidbits of lore relating to herself, her ancestry, or the town's history. Depending on your relationship level with Olive, different secrets will be revealed.

====0-32 Relationship Points====
*"I've been a Mortician for years! My poor—and quite dearly missed—husbands met some...unfortunate ends and I really felt a calling to the craft. You know, we're always looking for new recruits!"
*"My philosophy when it comes to décor is that if you're not making sure your place has personality, you're not ''living''. Or a [[ghost]] either. Not my point. But anyway, I'm sure some places have more [[personality]] than most. My house has a serious issue with flickering lights, doors slammed by someone other than [[Nervous Subject|Nyon]], and a TV that changes to static. It's odd, almost as if I'm haunted. Though why on earth should I be? My former husbands, all absolute dears, are resting quite peacefully!"

====33-65 Relationship Points====
*"[[Nervous Subject|Nyon]]'s been more distant with me these days. I guess that's just what happens with a lot of [[teen]]agers, but he's also been asking a lot of questions about [[Grim Reaper|his dad]] and about my past as well. Personally, I'd rather leave the past [[death|dead]] and buried. Wouldn't you?"
*"Because the [[graveyard|cemetery]] isn't far from me, I visit often. I feel like I'm quite acquainted with the dead, and it's calming to see the gravesites tended to. I'll often just peer into the pond. [[Layne Coffin|Layne]], though, he's gone straight for that pond when he's visited. He caught a frog out of it one night; peculiar little thing."
*"Have you seen that strange Bell Tower in Mourningvale? I'd heard once that people used to gather whenever someone rang its bell. I wonder if that's true? It makes me feel so odd whenever I walk past it."

====66-100 Relationship Points====
*"More than once, I've walked into a room to see [[Layne Coffin|Layne]] just staring at the TV. He's been transfixed by the Static TV channel. Wouldn't you think he has better things to do? He seems mesmerized by it."
*"Just before we moved to Crow's Crossing, we were warned that it's a little on the lively side. I have to say, we were not warned that a memorial cannon is occasionally fired. That might have been appreciated! I've chosen to stay away from that well not too far from us too; I've heard what sounded like a [[Edith|child]] shrieking or having some sort of tantrum last time I came close and I just thought, "You know what? I don't need a shrieking child in my life, thank you very much.""
*"I feel so bad about [[Zuleika Izadi|Zuleika]] dying like that, from her own [[Laganaphyllis simnovorii|plant]] no less! It's not like I lost her completely, but it's not the same to hang out with a [[ghost]]. Still, we try to talk whenever she stops back by [[Crow's Crossing]]. She doesn't ask a lot of questions about my past, which is very refreshing given, well, you know."

==Biography==
Olive appears alongside her son, [[Nervous Subject]], in [[Midnight Hollow]], one of the [[world]]s available for purchase from [[TheSims3.com#The Sims 3 Store|The Sims 3 Store]]. When the household is first played, she is 12 days away from aging up into an [[elder]].

There seems to be some kind of timeline confusion surrounding Nervous being taken away by [[social worker|social services]] and Olive's [[marriage]] to [[Ichabod Specter]]. In the [[Strangetown]] storyline from ''[[The Sims 2]]'', Nervous had already been taken away by the time she married Ichabod, and therefore before Ichabod's [[death]], whereas in Midnight Hollow, Ichabod is already dead and a ghost in her garden. Oddly, [[Earl E. DeMise]] does not appear in this world, although there is a [[gravestone|grave]] in the [[buydebug]] menu that reads "Reserved for Earl E. DeMise" and the description reads "''What's this about Easter Eggs?''" The family tree does not show who Nervous' father is, even though some evidence points to the fact that Nervous' father is the [[Grim Reaper]] in the family bio. This may be due to the Grim Reaper only being generated when needed.

As well as two [[skill]] points in [[cooking]], Olive also has two skill points in the [[Secret skill#Chess 2|chess]] and [[Secret skill#Diving|diving]] hidden skills, and one in the [[Secret skill#Collecting|collecting]] hidden skill.

==Biography==
Olive shares her eerie, haunted home with her niece, [[Ophelia Specter|Ophelia]]. Her sister, [[Willow Nigmos]] {{Nee|Muenda}}, and Willow's husband [[Creon Nigmos|Creon]] are both [[death|deceased]] and buried in [[List of Sims who died on the Specter lot|Olive's garden]]; their deaths are the result of [[drowning]]. She is the daughter of [[Lerato Muenda|Lerato]] and [[Peponi Muenda]], both also of [[Strangetown]], who both died in a [[fire]].  There is nothing to suggest these were acts of murder by this stage, as there was no motive, but there is a chance that the family name is cursed. "Muenda" means "To go" in Swahili.

Some time after several of her husbands' deaths, Olive tracked down the [[Grim Reaper]] to give him a piece of her mind, only to fall in [[relationship|love]] with him and they had [[WooHoo]], which suggests she had more than a passing relationship with death. [[Nervous Subject]] could be Grim Reaper's son. [[Resurrect-O-Nomitron|Paranormal career reward]], introduced in ''[[The Sims 2: University|University]]'', and calls the Grim Reaper, he will say that Olive doesn't know anybody who has died. This is because all the victims in her garden have unlinked character files.

Olive had a son - Nervous Subject - who was taken away by the [[Social Worker]]. There is no record of Nervous' father in the [[family tree]]. Nervous, now an [[adult]], currently resides at the [[Beaker family|Beaker]] residence with [[Loki Beaker|Loki]] and [[Circe Beaker]], who [[adoption|adopted]] him to perform experiments on him. Everyone expects Olive's money to be [[inheritance|inherited]] by Ophelia following her death, but, she might leave all her inheritance to her son, Nervous Subject.<ref>Since inheritance in ''[[The Sims 2]]'' is separate from family funds, the family funds will pass to Ophelia as long as she is living on the lot when Olive [[death|dies]].</ref><ref>If Olive significantly improves her relationship with Ophelia before she dies, there is a chance that some of the inheritance will go to her.</ref>

She dislikes [[General Buzz Grunt]], whose [[Lyla Grunt|ex-wife]] died on Olive's lot soon after leaving the [[Grunt family|Grunt household]]. 

When first played, Olive will have a [[Wants and Fears|want]] to [[pension|retire]]; because she has reached level 5 of the [[Slacker]] [[career]], Olive has a [[Career rewards#Slacker|Slacker career reward]] available for her to purchase. Although she has the correct [[skill]]s for her career level, she lacks the friends required. When the family is first played, she will be on her 10th day as an [[elder]].

During gameplay, she will eventually [[Death by old age|die from old age]], which is the same day that Ophelia will age up to an adult. Her relationships with Ophelia, Nervous Subject, and others will affect how much she leaves them, via her will. She will also pass away, on her property, allowing her to be kept in an [[gravestone|urn]], or perhaps buried on the property, with the multitude of other [[gravestone]]s.

==Olive's memory connections==
If one studies the chronology of Olive's [[memories]], it is apparent that she gave birth to her son [[Nervous Subject|Nervous]] after she had aged into an [[elder]]. Olive did [[WooHoo]] with the [[Grim Reaper]] after she became an elder. If one believes the theory that Grim Reaper is Nervous' father, that would mean that Olive got [[pregnancy|pregnant]] after she became an elder, which is not possible through normal gameplay.

==Olive's graveyard==
{{Main|List of Sims who died on the Specter lot}}
There are several people buried in Olive's backyard, along with family and former husbands - some of them are [[service]] people ([[maid]]s, [[delivery person|delivery people]], etc.). Many of them have names that are related to [[death]] (Euthanasia, Early Demise, Rigor Mortis, etc.) There are many theories about Olive, and many unknown questions, such as the causes for all of the deaths. Some players think perhaps that before the game was in stores, many Sims died. Many others believe they might be Olive's victims (despite murder technically being an impossibility in ''[[The Sims (series)|The Sims]]'' games) as a possible secret piece of her storyline. Olive's biography states that she will "stop at nothing to get what she wants." It also states that she spends her time "sharpening sticks," which may suggest her use of a weapon for her victims, and "excavating her yard," which gives the clue that she spends her time digging holes to bury the bodies of her victims. Her surname, [[Specter family|Specter]], is also related to death, as a specter is another term for a [[ghost]].
}}

==Trivia == 
*Olive's name might be a play on the phrase "I love specter," possibly showing her love of the [[Grim Reaper]].
*Olive's name could also be a play on "o-live", as in an 'alive specter', or a live [[ghost]] - possibly again a relation to the Grim Reaper.
*Olive, along with [[Herb Oldie|Herb]] and [[Coral Oldie]], is the only living [[Sim]] in ''[[The Sims 2]]'' base game that does not have grandparents in their [[family tree]].
*She remembers giving birth to a different [[Nervous Subject]] than the one that lives in [[Beaker family|Beaker household]].
*Like many people buried on her lot, she has no eyebrows.
*Olive has a hidden [[Fortune]] [[Aspiration (The Sims 2)|aspiration]] token, which can be viewed in [[Package editor#SimPE|SimPE]] along with her other [[memories]].
*On the official ''The Sims 2'' website, sometimes in the news, they would refer to Olive Specter's [[graveyard|cemetery]], but they call it Olive's garden. Sometimes it is called Olive's garden in-game, too. It could possibly be a reference to Olive Garden, which is thought to be a favorite restaurant for some of the game creators.
*Without the use of [[cheats]], the [[Elixir of Life]] or the [[Genie's lamp|Genie Lamp]], Olive [[Death by old age|dies of old age]] after about 2 days, the same day [[Ophelia Specter|Ophelia]] becomes an [[adult]].
*When editing her in SimPE, her natural hair color is determined as brown, though both her parents have black hair, and in the family's gallery, she is shown as an adult with black hair. This could be a mistake by the developers.
*In ''[[The Sims 3]]'', a medium painting can be the [https://postimg.cc/qgDdH002 picture] of Olive being left at the altar by [[Earl E. DeMise|Earl]]. It is a common [[Easter eggs|Easter egg]].
*Olive has no known [[relationship]]s with anyone in her graveyard except [[Ichabod Specter]], [[Lerato Muenda]], [[Peponi Muenda]], and [[Willow Nigmos]]. Strangely, each of these Sims are mere acquaintances with Olive despite being in her immediate family. They are also non-resurrectable. Using SimPE, you can see that she also has relationship points with 19 "Unknown" Sims. The remaining Sims in her graveyard appear to have relationship values, but they are not considered "known" relationships because the box is unchecked.
*Olive seems to have an obsession with [[death]]. An example would be her choice of spouses, Earl E. Demise (Early Demise), Rigger Mortis (Rigor mortis, the act of muscles stiffening after death), Hugh Thanasia (Pun on Euthanasia, the act of ending a life painlessly), etc. The hypothesis is supported by the past relationship she had with the Grim Reaper.
*Olive's bio suggests the possibility of her being a murderer and the people at her graveyard being her victims, as she spends her time "sharpening sticks and excavating her garden," and she will stop at nothing to get what she wants. 
**However, her unlucky [[trait]] in ''The Sims 3'' contradicts this and may imply that her husbands really did die from accidents and natural deaths.
*She lacks eyebrows in all iterations until her appearance in ''[[The Sims 4: Life & Death]]''.

==Biography==
In the [[Timeline of events in The Sims series#Alternate timeline|alternate timeline]] of ''The Sims 4'', Nervous Subject is known under his real name, Nyon Specter. This name change is explained by him not getting experimented on by the [[Beaker family]] yet in the alternate timeline. Neither has he been taken away by the [[Social Worker]] in the alternate timeline. The developers described him as "pre-Nervous," suggesting it takes place before he met the Beakers and became Nervous Subject.<ref>https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=DfV7shwdWus</ref> 

Nyon is a [[teen]], 21 days away from becoming a [[young adult]]. He lives in [[Crow's Crossing]] with his mother, [[Olive Specter|Olive]], and her fiancé, [[Layne Coffin]]. His father is the [[Grim Reaper]], as he has the [[Trait (The Sims 4)|Grimborn]] inherited trait, a trait automatically assigned to Grim's offspring (along with a scythe-shaped birthmark on their necks).

In this incarnation, Nyon possesses a darker skin tone to more accurately reflect his mother's genes. He maintains his signature mohawk hairstyle, albeit slightly more textured, while his lips and nose have been made fuller as well. 

When spoken to using the '''Ravenwood Rumors''' interaction, Nyon will mention once having a close friend named [[Pascal Curious|Pascal]] who suddenly and inexplicably moved away and wiped his [[Social Bunny (The Sims 4)|Social Bunny]] profile, which made the young man feel alone. This, in turn, led him to develop a friendship with the local town ghosts [[Alice]] and [[Edith]], whom most Sims would be terrified of. He has a good relationship with his mother but a neutral one with his soon-to-be stepfather, with a slight dip into the red. In fact, Nyon mentions he finds Layne weird, calling him a "creep".

==Social==
===[[file:Ravenwood Rumors.png|30px|link=]] Ravenwood Rumors===
Nyon, like other citizens of Ravenwood, has a special interaction called ''Ravenwood Rumors'' that reveals tidbits of lore relating to himself, his ancestry, or the town's history. Depending on your relationship level with Nyon, different secrets will be revealed.

====0-32 Relationship Points====
*"Hey, did you know you can catch these really cool Death Frogs around [[Ravenwood]]? I have the best luck in the cemetery. I love frogs, y'know. My mom jokes about how I'm a big collector of things. You can catch me around sometimes at festivals, even. Hit me up at Ravenwood Family Day and we'll talk frog."
*"My [[Layne Coffin|future stepfather]] is such a weirdo. Explain this: one day, the Sim's out by the crypt in [[Crow's Crossing]] looking at the gravesite for one of my mom's dead husbands. What is that all about? I saw him pat the headstone and smile affectionately. Creep alert!"

====33-65 Relationship Points====
*"Everybody seems to have theories about who my real dad is, like it's their business. The funny thing is, sometimes when I'm walking around, I'll see a weird reflection of a black cloak behind me. I feel a really strange tie to the idea of death and reaping. Wait, not creepy like that, I mean...well, just the idea of Grim is something, huh?"
*"The other day, the TV was on the fritz and it electrocuted me. Out of nowhere, there's Layne just standing there saying, "Watch yourself, kid, you'll die of electrocution if you're not careful" in this dreamy voice. I wonder if all his little fans know that the eccentric musician act is absolutely not an act."
*"[[Zelmira Gomes|Zelmira]] got way into that [[Tarot cards|tarot]] stuff a while back and got me all interested in the Order of Lenore stuff. You know about that, right? It was appealing to me, cuz I feel like I'm just always in some random danger that I can't predict or understand. Tarot gives me a sense of order, I think? Or it makes things feel less chaotic. Whatever, I just like it a lot. You've gotten cards and seen the tomes around Ravenwood and all that, right?"

====66-100 Relationship Points====
*"It probably seems weird but since there’s a lot of, uh, death in my family over time, even before I was around, I end up feeling pretty close to death. I mean, [[Olive Specter|mom]]’s career kinda adds to that. But what I mean is, I’m in those crypts a lot just wandering around and thinking. I’d say it’s a great place to get away from my soon-to-be-stepdad, but I can’t tell you how often I see him leaving the crypts right when I’m stopping by."
*"I’ve honestly been really lonely since my best friend [[Pascal Curious|Pascal]] moved. I mean the guy basically disappeared off the map! Deleted his [[Social Bunny]] and everything. It’s how I ended up talking to [[Edith]] so much. I kept going for walks all by myself and trying to talk to her. Not like I had anyone else, you know?"

====Layne's Secret Confession====
Once the player discovers ''Layne Coffin'''s secret, Nyon will have this to say;
*"You found out the truth about Layne, right? That guy's supposed to be my new dad. Yeah right! Like I want touching father/son moments with a freak-o-rama who ''wants'' my mom to turn him into a ghost. Uh, let's not unpack anything you think you know about my mom, okay? We're not touching that."

==Biography==
Nervous is no longer around except as a restless ghost in the main bedroom of [[Bella Goth]]'s mansion, [[Espiritu Estate]]. [[Emily Emory]] tells the player that Nervous was always short on money and signed up as a test subject for the Beakers. One day, [[Loki Beaker]] kept him in a miserable condition and performed a test on Nervous with one of the machine (presumably the [[Eclectic and Enigmatic Energizer]] as shown in the PC version). Unfortunately the machine he used shocked him to death. After Nervous' death, the Beakers even kidnapped a garbage man, [[Gimi Branko]], for their tests. The player has to obtain a charm from his grave and give it to [[Annie Howell]] at Nighthowl Saloon. It is indicated that he fell in love with Annie and became her boyfriend, but the player soon discovers that Annie is unaware of Nervous' death, and she admits that he left her. Nevertheless, she chooses to keep the charm, hinting that Nervous never stopped loving her. Nervous' ghost will leave Espiritu Estate forever after the player complete this task and then talk to Emily.

Nervous looks quite different in this game, while his outfit is similar, his hair is a bright reddish-yellow and his facial features look more normal and are far less customized, possibly due to the limitations of the PSP hardware.  

Despite only being a ghost, the game files reveal that he still has certain interests assigned to him, those being Politics, and, in contrast to his PC version, Crime and Environment.

==Biography==
Nervous Subject resides in [[Strangetown]] as an adult, and lives with the [[Beaker family]]. He has a black mohawk hairstyle and wears a gray T-shirt with a skeleton with loose bones on it, blue-gray jeans and sandals. He is 27 days away from being an elder. He is voiced by Stephen Kearin.

At one point during his early childhood, Nervous was taken away from his mother, [[Olive Specter]], by the [[social worker]]. According to his memories, he later moved in with [[Loki Beaker|Loki]] and [[Circe Beaker]], Strangetown's "mad scientist" couple, during his childhood. Although normal game mechanics would only allow this to happen through the [[adoption]] system, Nervous and the Beakers have no relation to each other on their [[family tree]], nor do the Beakers have memories of adopting him. They also would have been too young to adopt Nervous since he is almost as old as them, unless Loki and Circe had access to the [[Elixir of Life]], which is a possibility considering their reputation as mad-scientists.

Interestingly, Nervous' family tree only shows Olive as his mother, in contrast to the family trees of other pre-made Sims that typically display both parents. When looking through Olive's memories, it is revealed that the only individual she has a memory of [[WooHoo]] with is the [[Grim Reaper]]. Because of this, it is largely assumed that the Grim Reaper is Nervous' father, and this theory was confirmed in later games. Nervous lacks most of his mother's genetics; on closer examination, it is clear he is simply a clone of the Grim Reaper. Additionally, although [[Ophelia Nigmos]] is Nervous' cousin, they do not know one another when Strangetown is first played and erroneously lack family ties once they meet.

Nervous' bio states that Nervous twitches and blinks frequently, probably as a side effect from the Beakers experiments. He has the [[Family (aspiration)|Family]] aspiration, and when the Beakers' lot is first played, he will often roll wants to flirt or hug even though he will not like doing these things. He may also want to get married, which may be due to his aspiration being very low. For the first 7 or 8 game hours, the game will continually push "Stuff Face" actions on him while he is home, regardless of how hungry he is. This is a result of a script used for tutorial purposes, so he will see cockroaches (which are scripted as well since the house is fairly clean) and go into aspiration failure, unless the player diverts him away from them in time.

He does not appear to be very popular: his only friend is [[Pascal Curious]], although his lifetime relationship with him is only moderate. If ''[[The Sims 2: Nightlife|Nightlife]]'' is installed, he and Pascal will have good chemistry, leading to many fans pairing them together romantically. He also has a reasonably good relationship with Circe, but doesn't like Loki very much. Nervous will often wander onto the Curious lot when Pascal is about to give birth to his [[Tycho Curious|baby alien]].

According to Olive's memories, she was an elder when she had Nervous, which would not have been possible in normal gameplay. Additionally, her memories reveal a discrepancy about the ages of several Strangetown Sims. To illustrate, [[Lyla Grunt]] died before Nervous was born. However, this would mean the [[Grunt family|Grunt]] brothers should be older than Nervous. Nervous and the Beakers' memories are also inconsistent with their ages as all three remember Nervous moving in as a [[child]] despite him only being a few days younger than the Beakers. Hidden Nervous, on the contrary, remembers joining them as an adult, which would be more in line with the information [[Annie Howell]] provides the player about Nervous' life before his death in ''[[The Sims 2 (PSP)|The Sims 2]]'' for PSP.

All three [[Curious family|Curious brothers]] will falsely be flagged as family when opening Nervous' corresponding relationship data in [[Package editor|SimPE]], but they will not perceive each other as such in-game.

==Biography==
This version of '''Nervous Subject''' is hidden in the game files. He is also the Nervous who [[Olive Specter|Olive]] remembers giving birth to. He is unplayable. It is also unknown if the [[Grim Reaper]] is his father because Olive (and all of her family) has dark skin while Nervous' is light and the Grim Reaper has no genetics. He can be found using [[Package editor#SimPE|SimPE]] and he will have a second thumbnail in the [[Elder|Elder Stage]] hidden in his [[SimPE|character files]]. This Nervous appears in the storytelling images of the [[Beaker family]]. He also has [[memories]], which is unusual for a hidden Sim. Unlike his in-game counterpart, this Nervous remembers joining the Beaker family as an [[adult]].

Oddly he recognizes [[Willow Nigmos|Willow]] and [[Ophelia Nigmos]] as his aunt and cousin respectively and vice versa but does not 'know' them causing them to appear in the unrelated category in SimPE. The playable Nervous does not have relations to Willow and Ophelia.

The hidden Nervous starred in an old ''The Sims 2'' video Friday the 13th. Nervous is seen suffering throughout the day and ultimately died by satellite at the end of the video. In the said video, he has the [[teen]] male [[voice]] instead of the adult male voice.

Despite being a hidden Sim, Nervous also has [[memories]] that can be found in [[Package editor#SimPE|SimPE]].

==Trivia==
*Prior to the release of ''The Sims 2'', his original name was '''Nervous Beaker''', it was changed at some point during development.{{fact}}
*When displaying Nervous' gender preference in ''The Sims 2'' using [[testing cheats]] or checking in [[Package editor#SimPE|SimPE]], it can be seen that he has a slight distaste for women.
*In Grim's Ghastly Manor, a graveyard from ''The Sims 3'' Store designed to look like the home of the Grim Reaper, a [https://www.flickr.com/photos/94002117@N04/10348156426/ nursery] can be seen in the attic. This is possibly in reference to Nervous Subject as he is implied to be the Grim Reaper's son.
*His name in ''The Sims 4: Life & Death'', '''Nyon''', may be a play on "nigh on", meaning near in space, time, or relation. His full name would sound similar to "nigh on specter", aka ''nearly a specter'' or ''close to a specter''.
**This might be a reference to his fate in his PSP storyline.
*In ''The Sims 4: Life & Death'', Nyon has the '''Survived Seven Nights in a Haunted House'''{{vgversion|TS4:PS}} Milestone, though [[Haunted house residential|Haunted Houses]] are only available with ''[[The Sims 4: Paranormal Stuff|Paranormal Stuff]]''. Since the [[Crow's Crossing#Specter Family Manor|Specter Family Manor]] has the ''"On Hallowed Grounds"'' [[Lot traits and challenges|Lot trait]], it could mean that the house is meant to be a Haunted House.
* In the initial version of ''The Sims 4: Life & Death'', Nyon neither possessed the Grimborn trait nor did Grim appear on his family tree, though he was branded with the scythe-shaped birthmark. This was fixed with [[The Sims 4/Patch 173|Patch 173]], meaning he has the Grimborn trait in new saves.
